title: Multiplication in a single Koszul coordinate gives a distinguished triangle
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, r a natural number, g : Fin(r) -> A, i : Fin(r), and a,b in A. Let X=Spec(A) [def-pc-scheme] and fix D(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category]. For h : Fin(r) -> A, write K(h) for the Koszul complex [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], extended to cochain degrees -q, sheafified termwise, and localized in D(O_X). There exist arrows alpha:K(update(g,i,a)) -> K(update(g,i,a*b)), beta:K(update(g,i,a*b)) -> K(update(g,i,b)), and delta:K(update(g,i,b)) -> K(update(g,i,a))[1] forming a distinguished triangle. There is no regularity or positivity hypothesis on any generator.

source.place: Tag 09IR, displayed Koszul multiplication triangle; More on Algebra, Tags 062B and 062C. Read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09IR and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/062C (the TeX source is absent locally).

proof.text: For r=0 eliminate i:Fin(0). For r=s+1, let P be the extended Koszul complex on the remaining coordinates, indexed by i.succAbove. Apply the coordinate-cone isomorphism to a, b and a*b. Each is an isomorphism with the cone of the termwise sheafification of c times id_P.

Functoriality and the scalar composition law give mu(a) followed by mu(b) = mu(a*b). Mathlib HomotopyCategory.mappingConeCompTriangleh_distinguished gives the distinguished triangle of the cones of these composable endomorphisms. Apply the triangulated functor DerivedCategory.Qh.

Use DerivedCategory.Q.mapIso on the three coordinate-cone isomorphisms and compose with DerivedCategory.quotientCompQhIso to identify the exact three localized Koszul objects with the objects of the distinguished triangle. Transport its arrows by the object isomorphisms; Triangle.isoMk and Pretriangulated.isomorphic_distinguished prove that the transported triangle is distinguished.
